# SpeakX Social Studio — manager guide and delivery scope

## What is delivered

A complete October 2026 editorial plan, 31 draft Sia scripts with audio and channel directions, an automation architecture, and an interactive UI prototype. The attached prompts were treated as reference material, not as instructions to pause after every phase or publish content. No videos, audio renders, social posts, platform accounts or production agents have been created. The UI's character preview is explicitly a reference image.

## Decisions

- Sia is the only person visible and the only speaking voice in all videos. Other dialogue participants appear as text only. No background people, reflected people or separate actors.
- The user's location request overrides the fixed-studio restriction. Face, hair, outfit and voice remain locked. Scene backgrounds use approved map-linked locations.
- Use 35–45 second primary lessons rather than the other reference's 20–22 second generic Reels. Draft duration targets require a measured voice read; regenerate or shorten when pacing exceeds the slot.
- October contains 31 days, not the source document's 28-episode four-week sample.
- Daily primary lessons take priority over the other reference's lower default frequency. These are starting hypotheses, not proven best posting times.
- Every primary lesson runs on Instagram and Facebook. X gets two native text posts/day. Instagram gets one three-frame Story set/day. That is 155 scheduled units, or 217 individual videos, text posts and Story frames. No unplanned X video duplicates are included.
- Main slots: weekdays IG19:30/FB20:00 IST, weekends IG11:00/FB11:30 IST. X08:30/19:00 and Stories13:00 daily. UTC conversion must be generated from Asia/Kolkata, not by string replacement.
- Do not make unverified user-count, ranking, guaranteed learning or success claims. No paid spend is authorized by this plan.

## Use the prototype

1. Overview shows planned volumes and launch dependencies. Live posts and metrics remain empty.
2. Calendar opens all 31 days. Search by topic/location, filter status/level, and export CSV.
3. Open a lesson to read or edit script, location and IG/FB captions. The spoken copy is draft text, not generated audio.
4. In Review, send the lesson to demo review; change the role preview to Manager or Approver to approve; schedule the demo slot. Any saved edit clears approval, including changing the proposed time. This demonstrates interactions, not a secure approval gate.
5. Publishing queue shows demo scheduled lessons and local activity. Pause prevents scheduling demo slots. It never changes actual social accounts.
6. Agents shows role definitions and editable demo enable/disable settings. These are not executing services.
7. Reports defaults to no data. The optional illustrative example is explicitly fictional; download a report template for your first real week.
8. Maps accepts PNG/JPG/WebP images. Select a location and click to add a pin, then link it to an October lesson. Coordinates are normalized image positions, not latitude/longitude. Map art does not establish a real business address or imply Sia visited a real site.
9. Settings previews roles and exports a backup. Do not put credentials or personal information here.

## Prototype persistence and limits

Changes persist only in this browser's local storage. Role selection is a UI demonstration, not login or access control. Local drafts and map edits are not synchronized with other managers. The shared hosted prototype ships the same base calendar but every browser maintains its own edits. Production must use team login, server-enforced roles, durable database records and object storage. Browser uploads have a 2 MB image limit; keep backups. The prototype includes all 15 supplied Indian city maps with independent saved pins per map, plus one browser-uploaded map. Three conceptual Delhi example pins are supplied; the Interview Room is linked to October 1. Other pins are placed by the manager. The shared foreign folder was inspected and contains international maps and day/dusk/night subfolders; importing that larger library is a future expansion, not part of the 15-file India set. Replacing the browser-uploaded map requires confirmation before clearing its pins. Switching bundled city maps preserves their pins.

## Manager's daily routine

09:30: inspect overnight failures, token health, budgets and today's slots. 10:00: review packages, compare every platform crop and audio, request corrections with timestamps. By 12:00: final human approval of the exact media/caption/time/account version. Thirty minutes before the main slot: check readiness and pause any risky item. After posting: inspect permalinks and receipts. Next day: view first 24-hour snapshots. Never approve based only on a script when the video is still missing.

## Weekly production rhythm

Monday: inspect comparable prior-week results and approve one experiment. Tuesday: lock next-week briefs and unique words. Wednesday: language review, voice timing, scene selection. Thursday: render next week's package. Friday: human review, correction and scheduling. Weekend: short on-call checks, quiz moderation and emergency pause coverage. Keep three evergreen approved spare lessons; replacements require their own approved slot hash.

## Cost model to fill before commissioning media

31 lessons × 40 seconds ≈ 1,240 final voice/video seconds. Illustrative 1.5× render allowance = 1,860 generated seconds; three output crops are not automatically three separate identity generations. Estimate cost as model token cost + generated seconds × provider rate + rerenders + caption rendering + storage/egress + social API reads/writes + human review hours. Actual rates depend on provider/contract and must be quoted before spend. Alert at 80% of an approved budget; hold new generation at 100%. Limit to two regeneration attempts before a person decides. These are proposed controls, not a purchase instruction.

## Required inputs before production launch

Approved Sia voice/source video and provenance/consent record; map asset rights and accepted location pins; approved brand claims and destination links; social account ownership and app access; named primary/backup approvers; a production repository and deployment owner; media/API budget; reporting conversion events and privacy/retention rules. Missing accounts or media leave the relevant job blocked rather than fabricating success.
